literal_source_claim: Every semistable elliptic curve over Q is modular.
canonical_claim: For every elliptic curve E over the rational numbers, if E is semistable, then E is modular.
domain_and_universes: Elliptic curves over Q; the canonical source claim is not universe-polymorphic. A Lean representation and isomorphism-invariance boundary remain to be selected.
hypotheses: E is semistable at every finite place of Q
conclusion: E is modular in the source sense used by Wiles: its L-function is associated to a weight-two modular form (the exact conductor/newform normalization must be cross-checked before formal statement freeze).

alternate_encodings.target: compatibility of the two-dimensional Galois representation attached to E with that attached to a weight-two newform
equality of the elliptic-curve and modular-form L-series with matching conductor/level

excluded_degenerate_cases: Do not substitute all elliptic curves over Q, curves over a general number field, residual-representation modularity lifting, local good-or-multiplicative reduction at one DVR, or an abstract witness whose compatibility fields are unconstrained propositions. The source hypothesis is global semistability and the conclusion is genuine modularity.

source_revisions.primary_source: Andrew Wiles, Modular elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem, Annals of Mathematics 141 (1995), 443-551, Theorem 0.4, DOI 10.2307/2118559

foundation_profile: Lean 4 dependent type theory; classical logic and choice requirements remain open until the exact formal target and proof route are selected

freshness_and_revocation_policy: Invalidate on primary-source correction, change to the semistability or modularity boundary, Lean target, toolchain, dependency pins, assurance profile, or validator; independent review and review due date remain open.
